clue.text: Eminence achieved, despite indication of denial of competency

parts.note: the word not is the plain sign of a denial
competency is ability, the power to do something

explanation.surface: Someone rises to eminence even though they were told they were not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Notability is the state of being prominent or distinguished, which is what eminence means.

clue.text: In which a friend may prove his worth

definitions.text: In which a friend may prove his worth

parts.words: In which a friend may prove his worth
parts.note: the proverb says a friend in this situation is a friend indeed: the clue describes that state of want

explanation.surface: A remark on the testing of friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'a friend in need is a friend indeed' says true friends show themselves in times of want.

clue.text: Contribute something meagre without dispute

parts.note: to add a small extra to a deal or bargain as a free addition, with no argument over it

explanation.surface: Someone chips in a small amount and raises no objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To add something extra to a bargain at no charge, a small sweetener offered without haggling.

clue.text: Notices here there's slug in food provided

parts.note: a slug is a bullet, as fired from a gun
board is meals provided, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone finds a slug in the food they are served and wants to post a notice about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' suggests the garden creature; here it is the gun's bullet. BOARD is the food side of 'board and lodging'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noticeboard is where notices are pinned up for people to read.

clue.text: Crashed car — I'm all concerned, with tears

indicators.note: a crashed car is smashed up, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters I and M

explanation.surface: A driver who has crashed their car is all concerned and in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' signals the anagram of CAR, IM and ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrimal is the anatomical word for anything to do with tears, as in the tear glands.

clue.text: Almost all the force willing to go in for lashing

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the others
almost all of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: g is the symbol for the force of gravity
on means willing or game, as in 'are you on?'

explanation.surface: Most of the police force is keen to go in and take part in a whipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' reads as the police; it is g, the physics symbol. 'Almost all' trims the article, and 'in' places the willing word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a strip of leather, a lash used for whipping or binding.

clue.text: Yearn to be stretched out?

definitions.meaning: to yearn is to wish hard for something
something stretched out is extended in length

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether yearning means being stretched out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pine or desire; as an adjective it means extended or lengthy.

clue.text: Overhead and underground spot this, looking like insect's eyes

indicators.note: in a down clue the spot is put overhead, on top of the next piece

parts.note: a spot is a round mark, shaped like the letter O
a cellar is an underground room

explanation.surface: A spot seen above and below ground that looks like an insect's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelli are the simple eyes of insects, and the adjective describes things relating to or resembling them.

clue.text: Rescue pussy, and be favourably received

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Ding Dong Bell, pussy is in the well and must be fetched out from below
an idea that is welcomed by its audience

explanation.surface: Rescuing a cat earns someone a warm reception.
explanation.walkthrough: The British nursery rhyme 'Ding dong bell, pussy's in the well' supplies the first sense: to save the cat you climb into the well.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, descending a shaft to save the cat from the rhyme; idiomatically, to be well received or popular.

clue.text: Don't want to be a loner? Join up!

indicators.note: not wanting to stay as they are, the letters of the word loner change their arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to the lonely to join a club or the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't want to be' signals rearranging LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up as a member, the same as joining up.

clue.text: Beam at angry boss

parts.note: cross means angry
the head is the boss, the person in charge

explanation.surface: Someone smiles at an angry boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a verb, to smile; it is the noun, a bar of timber or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosshead is a transverse bar or beam, as at the top of a piston rod.

clue.text: Chaps in distress after the holidays — because of the food?'

indicators.note: after here means followed by, so the leave periods come next
letters in distress are disturbed and thrown about

parts.note: leaves are periods of holiday, as soldiers' leave

explanation.surface: Men come back from holiday feeling ill and blame what they ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' is the anagram signal; 'after' reads as 'followed by', so the holidays come second. 'Leaves' in the military sense is time off.
explanation.definitionFit: The leafy parts of the spinach plant are eaten as a green vegetable.

clue.text: Small noise made by boy -a cry of pain — in the arboretum

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a ping is a short ringing noise
Will is a boy's name, short for William
ow is what someone cries when hurt

explanation.surface: A boy gives a little cry of pain while out among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it names where this tree is found, not what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow with drooping branches, a typical specimen tree in a tree collection.

clue.text: For tying up the animal by its leg?

definitions.text: For tying up the animal by its leg?

parts.words: For tying up the animal by its leg?
parts.note: the clue reads a sailor's knot name literally, as a farm animal's lower leg used for tethering

explanation.surface: A question about tethering livestock by the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a knot used to shorten a rope, its name read here as a ewe's or ram's shank.

clue.text: Sounds convenient to have a hat, although it's of no advantage

indicators.note: Sounds says the first word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: handy means convenient
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A remark that wearing a hat is useful, though it brings no benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' covers only the word for convenient: the hat is spelt normally.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a disadvantage or hindrance, the opposite of a benefit.

clue.text: Vegetable essence?

definitions.meaning: a large green gourd grown in British gardens
the innermost or essential part of something, as in the pith of a matter

explanation.surface: A question whether a vegetable is the essence of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A large edible gourd; and the soft core of bone, figuratively the vital part of anything.

clue.text: Expressing approval since, strangely, it's medicine used legally

definitions.note: the adjective stands for the noun phrase, as in forensic medicine

parts.note: to be for something is to approve of it

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the word since are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone approves of medicine used in the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' is the anagram signal. Forensic is an adjective, but forensic medicine is the subject meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic medicine is medical science applied to questions of law, such as in court cases.

clue.text: Partly seen, Robert's attire

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Robert's clothes are only partly visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrobe is to dress or clothe, the verb sense of attire.

clue.text: Presented an account which might be altered

indicators.note: might be says the letters of the word altered could form a new word

explanation.surface: A report was given that might later be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to tell or narrate, so a story told is a story related.

clue.text: The twins in fine fettle, biographer found

annotationWithheld.why: The twins in fine fettle, biographer found: BOTH + WELL builds the answer, but Bothwell, husband of Mary Queen of Scots, was no biographer; the setter seems to have meant Boswell, so the definition is wrong for the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: The twins in fine fettle, biographer found

clue.text: Ten befuddled with liquor weave around

indicators.note: a befuddled mind is confused, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink, a liquor

explanation.surface: Ten people muddled by drink stagger about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' is the anagram signal, and fits a surface about drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or wind things together.

clue.text: Admitting Im a 'disgrace, with fleas hopping around most of 7 down

indicators.note: fleas hopping around jump in all directions, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: most of the 7 down answer is its underground room, its first letter dropped, and a basement is such a room

explanation.surface: A person confesses to disgrace, covered in fleas in an underground room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopping around' is the anagram signal. The 7 down answer without its first letter names an underground room; another word for that room completes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-abasement is humbling or degrading oneself, as in confessing one's own disgrace.

clue.text: With ingenuity, the French end up acquiring rotls!!

parts.note: art is skill or ingenuity

indicators.note: end up in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: Clever French people end up gaining something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end up' is a reversal signal in a down clue, where the piece reads upwards. A rotl is an Eastern weight, unfamiliar outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotl is a Middle Eastern unit of weight, and its plural takes this form.

clue.text: Look both ways

indicators.note: both ways says the word reads the same from either end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Advice to check left and right before crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick glance, a brief look.

clue.text: Medicine does taint horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a medicine spoils things horribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidotes are remedies that counteract poisons, a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Evil with love in its toils — that's what we hear

indicators.note: caught in the toils of something is trapped inside it

parts.note: vice is wickedness, evil
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Love is caught in the grip of evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in its toils' puts O inside VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice is the sound of a person speaking, which is what reaches our ears.

clue.text: Teases the youngsters

definitions.meaning: to tease is to rib or joke with someone

explanation.surface: Someone makes fun of the children.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means jokes with or ribs; as a noun it means children.

clue.text: Debars Uriah, the ne'er do well

parts.note: to black something is to ban or boycott it
Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: Uriah is shut out because he is a good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the creeping villain of Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A black sheep is the disreputable member of a family or group, a wastrel.
